- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, often overcorrects; cap peak forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or low values, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion tendency.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves when sentiment is >0.67; if model predicts drop, add 0.5–1% upward bias to counteract sentiment-driven overcorrection.
